title: Playing dances with Sonny Marshall and his Harlem Stompers
summary: With a car from his father he traveled to Newark and Passaic to play adult dances in Sonny Marshall's small combo, his first experience in a jazz group.

bands.name: Sonny Marshall and his Harlem Stompers

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Now, did many bands -- did many or any bands perform in Englewood at that time?

No, there weren't any bands performing in Englewood. I find that, when I started playing the bass fiddle, I used to -- oh, let's see, I was about at least -- oh, 15, 16, or possibly 17, I'd say. I used to travel to other towns like Newark, and I joined a little jazz combo. And by that time I was real, real hot and heavy and playing by ear, you know. And I joined this combo. They had heard about me.

So at that time Dad had given me a little car, and I was able to get around, you know, and I was, oh, traveling doing one nighters once in a while, as far as Newark, and Passaic and around -- let's see. The name of this outfit was called Sonny Marshall and his Harlem Stompers. It's something like that. It was a small combo, you know, five, six pieces.
What, did you play for dances? You played for dances?
Were these like adult dances or for teenage dances?
Well, it was adults, you know. And that was really the start of my trying to do something with the bass.

Now, when you were playing, were you playing -- when you were playing these jobs in Sonny Marshall's band, do you remember who -- what the other instrumentalists were, who they were, what instruments they played?

Right now it's going to be hard for me to remember. Oh, we had trombone. Trombone Red they used to call him. I forget his last name. And a drummer -- and Sonny Marshall, he played the alto sax. And we had a piano player, and I've forgotten some of the names of fellows, but that was really the start of my getting a little bit of experience, playing what you might say in a small combo, jazz or what you might say.
